fi-acreichthys-tomentosus.title: Aiptasia Eating Filefish
fi-acreichthys-tomentosus.summary: A small, camouflaged filefish from the Indo-West Pacific, widely kept to eat pest Aiptasia anemones. It can change color and texture to blend in.
rows: About 5.5 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 14 cm (5.5 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Omnivore. Foods: mysis shrimp, brine shrimp, chopped shrimp, squid and scallop, clam, krill, marine algae, marine pellets
Indo-West Pacific: Sri Lanka eastward thorough Indonesia to New Caledonia, north to southern Japan
notes: Once the Aiptasia is gone some individuals start picking at corals, polyps and other sessile invertebrates, so watch it closely in a reef.
